clue.text: Where one rides a rollercoaster? Just stop from flying off

parts.note: just means fair, as in a fair or just decision
to ground an aircraft is to stop it taking off

explanation.surface: A thrill-seeker on a rollercoaster fears being flung off the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair site with its rides is the place rollercoasters stand; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Elf-like creature, fine and insubstantial

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
airy means light and insubstantial

explanation.surface: A description of an elf as delicate and barely there.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairies and elves are both small magical folk of folklore, so one serves as a near synonym.

clue.text: End outside review regularly taken for bank's action to support currency

indicators.note: outside says the word for End goes around the letters taken from review

parts.note: an end is an aim or intention

indicators.note: regularly taken means every other letter of review is used

explanation.surface: A central bank winds up a review of its policy on propping up the currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly taken' keeps the odd letters of review; 'End' is a noun meaning aim, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When a central bank buys its own currency to prop it up, economists call that market intervention.

clue.text: Stick with left internally disheartened

indicators.note: internally says the letter for left goes inside the word for Stick

parts.note: to gum something is to stick it

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with the leftovers feels down inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum and disheartened are synonyms for gloomy and dejected.

clue.text: Cat English see in October

indicators.note: in says the English and see pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for October

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A cat-spotter's note: an English sighting this October.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Major newspaper owned by the state

definitions.meaning: a newspaper sold across the whole country
... also means state-owned, as in a nationalised industry

explanation.surface: A big paper that has been taken into public ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the country as a whole: a paper sold nationwide, and property held by the nation.

clue.text: Ominous feeling now chaps are trapped in it

parts.note: the present is now

indicators.note: are trapped in says the word for chaps sits inside the letters of it

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: A sense of dread as some men find themselves caught inside something.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a foreboding, a sense that something bad is about to happen.

clue.text: Very cowardly over avoiding the last round of fire

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, says the shortened word is turned upside down
avoiding the last means the final letter of the word for cowardly is dropped

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly

explanation.surface: A coward ducks out before the last burst of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding the last' drops the final letter of the word for cowardly before 'over' turns it upside down, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley is a simultaneous discharge of guns, one round of firing.

clue.text: Gatecrash home, beginning to turn abusive

parts.note: to be home is to be in

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of turn is used

parts.note: rude means abusive or offensive

explanation.surface: A party gatecrasher arrives at a house and starts turning nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to intrude, entering where one is uninvited.

clue.text: Part of the body needing some doctor's opinion

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An injured body part that calls for a medical view.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'needing', but that word is only the link joining definition to wordplay; 'Part of the body' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Uncovered cyan and navy thread

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of cyan are stripped away

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A spool of thread in two shades of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is spun fibre, a thread for knitting or weaving.

clue.text: Vast financial deficit in output from colliery

indicators.note: in says the deficit word sits inside the colliery output

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine, so its output is coal
a loss is a financial deficit

explanation.surface: A mine posts a huge loss on its production.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal and vast both mean enormous in size or extent.

clue.text: Magical symbol — place ten around

indicators.note: around signals the letters of place ten being moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a ritual: arrange ten things in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star used as a talisman in magic.

clue.text: Article concerning on that issue

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a particular matter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'There' can mean in that respect, as in 'I agree with you there'.

clue.text: Bird not finishing off the fly

indicators.note: not finishing off means the last letter of the is cut

parts.note: to fly is to rush or hurry

explanation.surface: A bird fails to catch the fly it is chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, a familiar garden species such as the song thrush.

clue.text: Anger some when accepting refusal

indicators.note: accepting says the word for some takes the refusal inside it

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Some people get angry when they are turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to annoy or irritate them; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Conclude with rebuke having finished

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A telling-off once someone has finally stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up a meeting or deal is to bring it to an end.

clue.text: Rubbish a Conservative's spinning

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A dismissal of a politician's spin as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory describes turning or rotating motion, as in a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Landing stage ripe for redevelopment

indicators.note: for redevelopment suggests the letters of ripe are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A property note: an old jetty ready to be redeveloped.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a platform built out over water where boats land passengers.

clue.text: Fanatical incursion capturing British

indicators.note: capturing says the raid word holds the British letter inside

parts.note: a raid is an incursion into enemy territory

explanation.surface: A zealous attack in which a Briton is taken prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid, used figuratively, means extreme or fanatical in one's views.

clue.text: Policeman with energy to get through

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A police officer finds the energy to get through a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or get by in difficult circumstances.

clue.text: Philosopher one found in short supply

indicators.note: found in says the numeral sits inside the shortened supply word
short means the last letter of the supply word is dropped

parts.note: stock is a supply of goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thinker is a rare find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STOCK to STOC, and 'found in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of the Greek school of Zeno, which taught calm endurance.

clue.text: Saw wanderer is in lead

indicators.note: is in says the wanderer word sits inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a rover is a wanderer

explanation.surface: Someone saw a wanderer out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, the same thing as a proverb.

clue.text: Firmly-established intense ocean trend regularly observed

parts.note: deep means intense, as in deep feeling
the sea is the ocean

indicators.note: regularly means only alternate letters of trend are kept

explanation.surface: A well-documented pattern in ocean conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of trend, giving TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-seated belief or problem is deeply rooted and hard to shift.
